mergePolicy: Merge only records that describe the same underlying defect, root cause, affected path, or materially identical remediation. Preserve the highest source severity while retaining every member's original severity, evidence, locations, impact, remediation, verification guidance, and source pointer.

clusters.title: Four live credentials and a sensitive local endpoint are committed
clusters.rationale: Both records cite the same four exposed values in the same tracked local-tool files and require the same rotate, untrack, history-rewrite, and secret-scanning remediation.
clusters.preserve: Keep configuration/reproducibility impact, security exploitability, endpoint/permission context, provider-log review, and full-history cleanup requirements.

clusters.title: App and widget lack required-reason privacy manifests
clusters.rationale: Both records describe the same absent app and widget PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy files, the same covered first-party APIs, and the same per-target required-reason declarations.
clusters.preserve: Keep target-membership evidence, exact reason-code guidance, archive inspection, Organizer privacy report, and App Store validation impact.

clusters.title: CI selects an impossible and internally conflicting iOS 26 toolchain
clusters.rationale: All three records trace to Xcode 16.1 plus the Makefile DEVELOPER_DIR override while the project requires the iOS 26 SDK/runtime. They share the same preflight and Xcode 26 remediation.
clusters.preserve: Keep build-gate, privacy/release-validation, and test-execution consequences, plus the distinction that this proves CI invalidity rather than source failure under Xcode 26.

clusters.title: No committed shared scheme or test plan defines the CI test action
clusters.rationale: Both records cite the same absent shared scheme/test plan, reliance on xcuserdata/autogenerated behavior, and lack of a portable target-selection contract.
clusters.preserve: Keep project-configuration reproducibility and testing target/count/coverage impacts.

clusters.title: Release, analyzer, archive, and distribution-signing behavior is not gated
clusters.rationale: Both records identify the same Debug-only CI path and absent Release/analyze/archive/sign/export verification, with materially identical release-lane remediation.
clusters.preserve: Keep Release compiler/settings, widget embedding, sanitizer/analyzer, entitlement/profile, dSYM, signing, export, and App Store validation impacts.

clusters.title: Tracked local, generated, user-state, log, and backup artifacts defeat repository hygiene
clusters.rationale: The three records describe the same tracked artifact set and the same untrack/ignore/sanitized-artifact remediation; the dead-code report adds the quantified manifest.
clusters.preserve: Keep exact artifact counts, stale-build/reproducibility risk, developer-path/privacy exposure, log-retention guidance, and the separate reference to credential rotation for the local configs.

clusters.title: Info.plist claims Live Activity support without an Activity configuration
clusters.rationale: Both records cite NSSupportsLiveActivities with no ActivityKit import, attributes, lifecycle, or ActivityConfiguration and prescribe removal or full implementation.
clusters.preserve: Keep capability-metadata drift, release-review, Lock Screen/Dynamic Island, and physical-device verification context.

clusters.title: The app carries an unused APNs capability
clusters.rationale: Both records cite the same aps-environment entitlement with no push registration/token/product path and require removing Push Notifications or implementing it fully.
clusters.preserve: Keep least-privilege, provisioning/signing drift, App Group preservation, and final signed-archive entitlement verification.

clusters.title: Listening-session tracking exists but is never wired into production
clusters.rationale: Both records cite the same nil sessionService/configuration gap in the production service graph and the same configureSessionTracking remediation after the schema fix.
clusters.preserve: Keep downstream history, play-count, rediscovery, recommendation, smart-search, preview/fallback construction, and required-dependency guidance.

clusters.title: Concurrent import deduplication has a check-to-insert race
clusters.rationale: Both records describe identical cache snapshots and non-atomic actor-isolated existence checks allowing duplicate copy and Track creation.
clusters.preserve: Keep batch-local in-flight claim, persistence-level uniqueness/create-if-absent, alias handling, failure release, and concurrency-test requirements.

clusters.title: Every pagination request hydrates the full result set to compute an unused count
clusters.rationale: Both records cite the same pagination helpers and whole-dataset model fetch used as a count on every page while the UI does not consume totalCount.
clusters.preserve: Keep large-library complexity, near-quadratic cumulative work, store-side count option, includeTotalCount=false fast path, and 50k-row profiling requirements.

clusters.title: Listening-session replacement is unsequenced and can clear the new session
clusters.rationale: Both records identify the same unstructured old-session teardown in ListeningSessionService that reads and clears mutable replacement state.
clusters.preserve: Keep the broader transition omissions for Next/Previous/auto-advance, exact start-A/start-B race, ordered replacement contract, and playback-lifecycle test matrix.

clusters.title: Import cancellation does not propagate to AsyncStream producers
clusters.rationale: Both records cite discarded unstructured producer tasks, absent continuation.onTermination, and continued discovery/copy/persistence after the consumer reports cancellation.
clusters.preserve: Keep discovery and processing producers, buffer/yield behavior, copy cancellation limit, cleanup, security-scoped access, and deterministic post-cancel assertions.

clusters.title: Queue edit callbacks translate visible offsets to the wrong absolute indices
clusters.rationale: Both records describe the same currentIndex+1 base error for displayed Up Next delete/move operations and the same queue API/index-translation remediation.
clusters.preserve: Keep end-destination and multi-delete semantics plus the separate UI discoverability/edit-mode impact.

clusters.title: Sleep-timer ownership is transient and fade volume starts from 1.0
clusters.rationale: Both records cite the same NowPlayingContent-owned SleepTimerManager and hard-coded full-volume baseline, with the same persistent-owner and authoritative-volume remediation.
clusters.preserve: Keep dismissal/background/relaunch lifetime, fade jump, cancel/restore semantics, absolute expiry, and single-fire verification.

clusters.title: Audio diagnostics report synthetic zero metrics while polling an empty collector
clusters.rationale: Both records cite AudioKitEngineAdapter fixed-zero metrics and empty collection, producing false healthy diagnostics while paying polling overhead.
clusters.preserve: Keep native-adapter synthetic metric concerns, unsupported-versus-zero modeling, diagnostic scores/exports, output-tap gating, and device instrumentation requirements.

clusters.title: Widget synchronization is stale and poll-driven
clusters.rationale: All three records describe the same widget synchronization path: frozen elapsed time/stale state and a 500 ms MainActor queue poll that still misses mode-only changes. They share an event-driven snapshot/timestamp/rate remediation.
clusters.preserve: Keep progress projection, stale-playing policy, shuffle/repeat propagation, playback-rate correctness, bounded App Group writes, idle/background energy cost, and lifecycle teardown.

clusters.title: Primary library and mini-player actions use raw gestures instead of semantic controls
clusters.rationale: Both records identify the same onTapGesture action surfaces in overlapping library paths and prescribe native Button/NavigationLink or explicit default actions.
clusters.preserve: Keep general interaction semantics, compound Play/Info row design, mini-player Open Now Playing action, VoiceOver, keyboard, Switch Control, and Voice Control impact.

clusters.title: The 10-band EQ is a drag-only, undersized, non-adjustable control
clusters.rationale: Both records cite the same VerticalSlider implementation, fixed 30-point width, DragGesture-only input, and missing adjustable/focus/keyboard semantics.
clusters.preserve: Keep narrow-layout reachability, 44-point hit area, frequency/dB labels, 0.5 dB steps, native-versus-custom implementation options, and all assistive-input tests.

clusters.title: Accessibility, Dynamic Type, locale, RTL, and widget behavior lack a real verification lane
clusters.rationale: Both records identify the same absent accessibility audit/configuration coverage and the same automated audit plus manual device-matrix remediation.
clusters.preserve: Keep skip-on-missing behavior, stable identifiers, AX5/RTL configurations, widget coverage, focus/order, contrast, Reduce Motion/Transparency, Switch Control, and physical-device limits.

clusters.title: Surprise Me lacks a single-flight gate for its shared model session and playback side effects
clusters.rationale: Both records share the same enabled repeated action and existing busy state. One records queue/playback races; the other records the same overlap violating the shared LanguageModelSession single-request contract.
clusters.preserve: Keep progress UI, action disablement, admission gate, isResponding/fresh-session option, exact one queue/playback side effect, and eligible-device runtime uncertainty.

clusters.title: Failures are collapsed into silence, false emptiness, or generic fallback states
clusters.rationale: The Foundation Models record is the Smart Search/model-status slice of the broader UI failure-state defect: distinct failures are discarded and SearchView does not render its error state. Both require typed state and user-safe reason preservation.
clusters.preserve: Keep audio initialization, Home, standard search, File Manager, Foundation Models availability reasons, asset loss, locale, guardrail, context, cancellation, privacy-safe logging, and retry/recovery distinctions.

clusters.title: Persisted EQ is not restored or reapplied across engine creation and switching
clusters.rationale: DCA-PART-002 is the persisted-EQ subset of AUD-DSP-001 and cites the same facade/helper/engine-switch gap with the same load-and-apply remediation.
clusters.preserve: Keep the broader engine capability/replay-gain divergence, one authoritative EQ state, cold launch/recreation/auto-advance coverage, and unsupported-engine UI state.

clusters.title: Visible audio settings persist values but do not configure the active audio engine
clusters.rationale: AUD-CONFIG-001 is the bit-perfect/buffer/sample-rate subset of the broader inert-settings record and shares the same defaults-only, no-runtime-consumer root cause.
clusters.preserve: Keep the additional inert appearance/haptics/file actions, authoritative effective-value UI, source-rate wording, buffer application, route sample-rate verification, and remove-until-real option.

clusters.title: Now Playing lacks an adaptive scroll/layout contract for short heights and Dynamic Type
clusters.rationale: Both records cite the same non-scrollable NowPlayingContent stack, unused size category, fixed artwork/spacers, and lower-control reachability under landscape or accessibility sizes.
clusters.preserve: Keep Home-card fixed-height clipping, line wrapping, compact accessibility layouts, actual scroll content, safe-area behavior, long strings, pseudolanguage, and AX5 device matrix.

clusters.title: Missing prerequisites and behavior are converted into passing test skips
clusters.rationale: TRV-004 is the UI-test subset of TRV-015's repository-wide skip problem. Both allow core missing behavior to pass and require deterministic prerequisites plus failure on unexpected skips.
clusters.preserve: Keep UI postconditions and identifiers, AudioKit/App Group/widget prerequisites, 26-site inventory, silent early returns, xcresult skip gate, lane-specific allowlist, and owner/expiry governance.

nearDuplicateNonMerges.reason: DLP-003 is a production migration-plan defect; TRV-010 is the independent absence of a real migration test. One can be fixed while the other remains.
These share Smart Search files but are four different defects: mode reachability, stale cancellation writes, fallback handoff, and playback action integration.
Toolchain incompatibility prevents CI execution; missing Release/archive gates remain a separate contract even after the toolchain is corrected.
CP-012 includes unbounded sample/error retention and a separate no-op poller lifecycle. CAN-016 covers false synthetic metrics; merging would hide the independent memory-growth issue.
DLP-005 is compensating cleanup after a copied-file failure. CAN-013 is missing task cancellation propagation; either can occur without the other.
Unwired tracking, replacement teardown races, and incorrect listened-duration measurement are separate lifecycle layers with distinct fixes.
Bit-perfect path verification and synthetic diagnostic metrics are related trust problems but have different owners, evidence, and acceptance tests.
Missing ListeningSession schema registration and the migration-plan-open sequence are separate persistence defects.
A missing committed test action and aliases that fail to select unit/UI targets require separate changes even though both affect test selection.
Coverage evidence quality and Release/archive gating are independent release controls.
The semantic-control defect and the missing accessibility verification lane are implementation versus test-coverage findings.
A missing visible dismissal action and missing scroll/reachability contract affect the same screen but have independent controls and fixes.
Stale cancellation writes and failure-to-handoff fallback are separate Smart Search state-machine defects.
Credential rotation/history purge must remain separate from general artifact cleanup; untracking files alone does not revoke secrets.
The production gapless/crossfade implementation defect and absence of output verification are code behavior versus evidence-lane findings.
M4A misclassification and mismatch between advertised/imported formats and detector representation have different affected inputs and remediations.
